what: Apple's exact sentences relied on for the iOS 26 record, as captured on 26 September 2026. Sentences over 300 characters are shown as an excerpt (quote_is_excerpt); quote_sha256 is always the fingerprint of the full sentence. 'paraphrase_claude' and 'claude_note' are Claude's words, not Apple's.

E01.quote: To turn off Siri, go to Settings > Siri > Talk to Siri and tap Off, and go to Settings > Siri > Talk to Siri and tap to turn off “Press Home for Siri” or “Press Side Button for Siri”.
E01.locator: To turn off Siri, go to Settings > Siri > Talk to Siri
E01.paraphrase_claude: Apple defines turning off Siri as Talk to Siri Off plus Press Side (or Home) Button for Siri off.

E02.quote: To turn off Dictation, go to Settings > General > Keyboard, then tap to turn off Enable Dictation.
E02.locator: To turn off Dictation, go to Settings > General > Keyboard
E02.paraphrase_claude: Dictation is turned off with Enable Dictation in Keyboard settings.

E03.quote: If you turn off both Siri and Dictation, the transcripts of your Siri and Dictation requests that are stored on your device and used to personalize your experience will be deleted.
E03.locator: If you turn off both Siri and Dictation
E03.paraphrase_claude: On-device transcripts used for personalisation are deleted only when both Siri and Dictation are off.

E04.quote: You can delete the transcripts of your Siri and Dictation requests that are stored on your device by going to Settings > Siri > Siri & Dictation History and tapping Delete Siri & Dictation History.
E04.locator: You can delete the transcripts of your Siri and Dictation requests
E04.paraphrase_claude: Delete Siri & Dictation History removes transcripts stored on the device.

E05.quote: When you use Siri and Dictation, your device may send other contextual data to Apple, including from third-party apps you allow to integrate with Use with Siri Requests, such as:
E05.locator: your device may send other contextual data to Apple
E05.paraphrase_claude: When Siri and Dictation are used, the device may send contextual data to Apple, including from third-party apps allowed via Use with Siri Requests.

E06.quote: Contact names, nicknames, and relationships (for example, “my dad”), if you set them up in your contacts
E06.paraphrase_claude: Contextual data list: contact names/nicknames/relationships, form of address, music and podcasts, device names, Home names, item labels (Photos people, alarms, Reminders lists), installed apps and Siri shortcuts.

E07.quote: You can control which apps can integrate with Allow Siri Requests at any time by going to Settings > Siri > Apps > [app name] > Use with Siri Requests.
E07.locator: You can control which apps can integrate with Allow Siri Requests
E07.paraphrase_claude: Per-app control of which apps integrate with Siri requests (named both Allow Siri Requests and Use with Siri Requests).

E08.quote: To stop apps from contributing information to personalize Siri, go to Settings > Siri > Apps > [app name], then tap to turn off Learn from this App.
E08.locator: To stop apps from contributing information to personalize Siri
E08.paraphrase_claude: Learn from this App, per app, stops that app contributing information to personalise Siri.

E09.quote: To stop app clips from contributing information to personalize Siri, go to Settings > Siri > App Clips and tap to turn off Learn from App Clips.
E09.locator: To stop app clips from contributing information
E09.paraphrase_claude: Learn from App Clips stops app clips contributing to Siri personalisation.

E10.quote: If you do not want Siri Suggestions in apps, or when sharing, searching, or listening, you can disable Siri Suggestions by going to Settings > Siri and tapping to turn off “Show in App Library”, “Show in Spotlight”, “Show When Sharing”, or “Show When Listening”.
E10.locator: If you do not want Siri Suggestions in apps
E10.paraphrase_claude: Apple says Show in App Library / Spotlight / When Sharing / When Listening disable Siri Suggestions in those places.

E11.quote: Siri Suggestions uses local, on-device processing to learn how you use your devices and apps in order to personalize your experience.
E11.locator: Siri Suggestions uses local, on-device processing
E11.paraphrase_claude: Siri Suggestions learns on the device how you use devices and apps.

E12.locator: such as your Safari browsing history, emails, messages, images, notifications, and contacts

E13.locator: If you do not want Siri personalization to sync

E14.paraphrase_claude: Siri settings and Suggestions personalisation sync across devices via iCloud (end-to-end encrypted).

E15.locator: the audio from when you set up Siri to recognize your voice

E60.quote: … and, if you opted in to Personal Requests on HomePod, phone call status, …
E60.locator: and, if you opted in to Personal Requests on HomePod, phone call status,
E60.paraphrase_claude: Scope decision: in_scope. The opt-in concerns HomePod, but Apple's sentence says what is shared is phone call status 'from your device', i.e. this iPhone's data, and it is the only condition Apple attaches to that part of the nearby-device flow (E29/N05). Excluding it would leave the phone-call-status part of nearby_device_status wrongly recorded as having no switch. Apple gives no Settings path and does not say whether the opt-in is made on the iPhone (for example in the Home app) or on HomePod; settings_path is null for that reason. Grid effect: stops = the phone-call-status part of nearby_device_status (on opt-out); timers, alarms, shared media and proximity are not tied to it.

E62.quote: To change how Siri accesses your information, go to Settings > Siri & Search.
E62.locator: To change how Siri accesses your information, go to Settings > Siri & Search.
E62.paraphrase_claude: Apple names a settings location, not a switch, so kind is 'settings_pane' (new kind; no existing kind fits). It concerns Siri Suggestions (Today at Apple session suggestions), so in_scope. 'Settings > Siri & Search' is probably the older name of the pane that ask-siri-dictation calls 'Settings > Siri', but Apple does not say so; record it as a wording issue (fifth way of naming the Siri settings root) and do not grid it, since no switch or effect is named. The ask-siri-dictation page has a parallel pane-level control ('see and control the full list of features that Siri personalizes ... by going to Settings > Siri') that is also not in switches.json; not on the checker's list, noted here only.

E65.quote: … Alerts & Shortcuts Automations: Your iPhone and Apple Watch will use your location …
E65.locator: Alerts & Shortcuts Automations: Your iPhone and Apple Watch will use your location
E65.paraphrase_claude: Scope decision: adjacent. Apple describes 'an app or shortcut recommendation based on where you currently are', which resembles Siri Suggestions ('Siri can suggest shortcuts', E12), but this page never names Siri or Siri Suggestions, and says the iPhone 'will use' your location, not that it is sent to Apple.
